claim: The basal forebrain cholinergic system projects broadly throughout the cortex and constitutes a critical source of neuromodulation for arousal and attention.
source: The basal forebrain cholinergic system projects broadly throughout the cortex and constitutes a critical source of neuromodulation for arousal and attention.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific understanding of the basal forebrain cholinergic system's role in neuromodulation.

claim: Recent studies have revealed a high degree of spatiotemporal specificity in cholinergic signaling.
source: However, recent studies have revealed a high degree of spatiotemporal specificity in cholinergic signaling.
evidence: This claim references recent studies without specific citations in this sentence, but is supported by citations elsewhere in the manuscript.

claim: Cholinergic fibers within the mouse cortex exhibit remarkable laminar and regional specificity organized in accordance with cellular birthdate.
source: Here, using intersectional genetic fate mapping, we demonstrate that cholinergic fibers within the mouse cortex exhibit remarkable laminar and regional specificity and that this is organized in accordance with cellular birthdate.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data using intersectional genetic fate mapping.

claim: Birthdated cholinergic projections within the cortex follow an inside-out pattern of innervation.
source: Strikingly, birthdated cholinergic projections within the cortex follow an inside-out pattern of innervation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Early born cholinergic populations target deep layers while late born ones innervate superficial laminae.
source: While early born cholinergic populations target deep layers, late born ones innervate superficial laminae.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating and projection mapping experiments.

claim: Birthdate predicts cholinergic innervation patterns within the amygdala, hippocampus, and prefrontal cortex.
source: We also find that birthdate predicts cholinergic innervation patterns within the amygdala, hippocampus, and prefrontal cortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Acetylcholine plays an essential role in modulating attention, motivation, and learning within neocortical, hippocampal, and subcortical circuits.
source: Acetylcholine (ACh) plays an essential role in modulating attention, motivation, and learning within neocortical, hippocampal, and subcortical circuits (Ballinger et al., 2016; Luchicchi et al., 2014; Picciotto et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The primary source of ACh within neocortical, hippocampal, and subcortical structures are projection neurons located in several nuclei throughout the basal forebrain.
source: The primary source of ACh within these structures are the projection neurons located in several nuclei throughout the basal forebrain.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about the source of acetylcholine in the brain.

claim: Historically, basal forebrain cholinergic neurons were thought to be relatively indiscriminate sources of ACh, releasing it slowly and diffusely throughout the cortex.
source: Historically, these neurons were thought to be relatively indiscriminate sources of ACh, releasing it slowly and diffusely throughout the cortex to mediate widespread circuit activation (Sarter et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research describing the historical view.

claim: In vitro work has implied a multitude of layer-, cell type-, and synapse-specific cholinergic effects.
source: Nonetheless, considerable in vitro work has implied a multitude of layer-, cell type-, and synapse-specific cholinergic effects (reviewed in Muñoz and Rudy, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Recent in vivo findings have revealed an even higher level of spatiotemporal coordination in cholinergic signaling.
source: Recent in vivo findings have revealed an even higher level of spatiotemporal coordination (Froemke et al., 2007; Muñoz et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent in vivo studies.

claim: The ACh system is composed of distinct cell types that target specific layers and circuit elements of the cortex in a temporally precise manner.
source: These observations hint that the ACh system is composed of distinct cell types that target specific layers and circuit elements of the cortex in a temporally precise manner.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observations mentioned in the previous sentences.

claim: Basal forebrain cholinergic neurons have been divided into four groups based upon cell body location: Ch1 (medial septum), Ch2 (vertical diagonal band), Ch3 (horizontal diagonal band), and Ch4 (substantia innominata and nucleus basalis).
source: Classically, the basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (BFCNs) have been divided into four groups based upon cell body location – Ch1 (medial septum), Ch2 (vertical diagonal band), Ch3 (horizontal diagonal band), and Ch4 (substantia innominata and nucleus basalis) (Mesulam et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a classical study.

claim: The broad anatomical divisions of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons roughly reflect their innervation of different brain structures (i.e. neocortex, hippocampus, and amygdala).
source: These broad anatomical divisions roughly reflect their innervation of different brain structures (i.e. neocortex, hippocampus, and amygdala).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the organization of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons.

claim: Early work suggested that rostrally located cholinergic cells project to medial cortical areas and that caudal cells project laterally.
source: Early work suggested that rostrally located cells project to medial cortical areas and that caudal cells project laterally (Baskerville et al., 1993; Saper, 1984).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to early studies.

claim: Early work on cholinergic topography was primarily carried out using anterograde and retrograde tracers which allowed the broad spatial topography to be determined, but could not distinguish between cholinergic and noncholinergic cells.
source: This work was primarily carried out using anterograde and retrograde tracers which allowed the broad spatial topography to be determined, but could not distinguish between cholinergic and noncholinergic cells.
evidence: This is a description of the methods and limitations of early work, based on knowledge of those techniques.

claim: Recent genetic tools have allowed for the sparse, selective targeting of cholinergic cell types but failed to reveal their overall topographic and anatomical organization.
source: More recently, genetic tools have allowed for the sparse, selective targeting of cholinergic cell types but failed to reveal their overall topographic and anatomical organization (Li et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2014; Zaborszky et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies using genetic tools.

claim: Using a hybrid genetic/retrograde labeling strategy demonstrates the existence of cholinergic neurons with specific projections to deep, middle, and superficial layers of the mouse somatosensory cortex.
source: Here, by using a hybrid genetic/retrograde labeling strategy, we demonstrate the existence of cholinergic neurons with specific projections to deep, middle, and superficial layers of the mouse somatosensory cortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: All cholinergic neurons in the forebrain originate within the Nkx2.1+ proliferative region of the ventral embryonic telencephalon.
source: It is known that all cholinergic neurons in the forebrain originate within the Nkx2.1+ proliferative region of the ventral embryonic telencephalon (Marin et al., 2000; Patel et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The diversity of other cell types arising from the Nkx2.1+ region is generated by both spatially defined progenitor pools and temporal shifts in the neuronal subtype produced.
source: The diversity of other cell types arising from this region is generated by both spatially defined progenitor pools (Gelman et al., 2009; Nóbrega-Pereira et al., 2010; Wonders et al., 2008), as well as temporal shifts in the neuronal subtype produced (Inan et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on cell type diversity.

claim: The temporal, but not the spatial, organization of the progenitors predicts the organization of the mature cholinergic projections.
source: Here, we investigated the developmental origins of cholinergic projection neuron topography. We were surprised to find that the temporal, but not the spatial, organization of the progenitors predicted the organization of the mature cholinergic projections.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from spatial and temporal fate mapping.

claim: The axons of cholinergic neurons born at different embryonic timepoints take distinct pathways to reach their projection targets.
source: Furthermore, we found that the axons of cholinergic neurons born at different embryonic timepoints take distinct pathways to reach their projection targets.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from pathway analysis.

claim: The ChatFlpO mouse line exhibits the expected selectivity of FlpO expression within cholinergic neurons when crossed to a pan-ventral (Dlx6aCre) line and visualized using an intersectional reporter (Rosa26Ai65).
source: This mouse line exhibits the expected selectivity of FlpO expression within cholinergic neurons when crossed to a pan-ventral (Dlx6aCre) line and visualized using an intersectional reporter (Rosa26Ai65) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CAV-2::Cre virus specifically infects axon terminals.
source: This virus specifically infects axon terminals (Ekstrand et al., 2014; Junyent and Kremer, 2015), resulting in Cre expression only in cells that innervate the injected region.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on CAV-2::Cre properties.

claim: The majority of cholinergic projections were restricted to the injected layers in the somatosensory cortex.
source: Using this method, we observed that the majority of projections were restricted to the injected layers.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from CAV-2::Cre injections.

claim: Most cholinergic neurons predominantly arborize within specific cortical laminae.
source: This indicates that most cholinergic neurons predominantly arborize within specific cortical laminae (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Deep layer injections largely showed projections restricted to layers 5 and 6 (L5-6) of the somatosensory cortex.
source: In particular, deep layer injections largely showed projections restricted to layers 5 and 6 (L5-6) of the somatosensory cortex, whereas superficial injections primarily showed projections within layers 1 through 4 (L1-4), with some showing remarkable specificity for L1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from layer-specific CAV-2::Cre injections.

claim: Superficial layer injections primarily showed projections within layers 1 through 4 (L1-4), with some showing remarkable specificity for L1.
source: In particular, deep layer injections largely showed projections restricted to layers 5 and 6 (L5-6) of the somatosensory cortex, whereas superficial injections primarily showed projections within layers 1 through 4 (L1-4), with some showing remarkable specificity for L1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from layer-specific CAV-2::Cre injections.

claim: There is a bias for deep layer-projecting cholinergic cells to be predominantly located in more caudal structures (Bregma −2.0 to −0.5, corresponding to the NB and caudal SI).
source: We did note, however, that there is a bias for deep layer-projecting cells to be predominantly located in more caudal structures (i.e. Bregma −2.0 to −0.5, corresponding to the NB and caudal SI), while superficially projecting cells are enriched in more rostral BF structures (Bregma −0.5 to +0.5, corresponding to the hDB and rostral SI) (ANOVA, F(2,18) = 13.63, p=0.0037, see Supplementary file 1 for ANOVA summary tables).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis (ANOVA).

claim: Superficially projecting cholinergic cells are enriched in more rostral BF structures (Bregma −0.5 to +0.5, corresponding to the hDB and rostral SI).
source: We did note, however, that there is a bias for deep layer-projecting cells to be predominantly located in more caudal structures (i.e. Bregma −2.0 to −0.5, corresponding to the NB and caudal SI), while superficially projecting cells are enriched in more rostral BF structures (Bregma −0.5 to +0.5, corresponding to the hDB and rostral SI) (ANOVA, F(2,18) = 13.63, p=0.0037, see Supplementary file 1 for ANOVA summary tables).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis (ANOVA).

claim: Embryonic progenitor zone origin has been shown to predict subtype identity within other forebrain lineages.
source: Embryonic progenitor zone origin has been shown to predict subtype identity within other forebrain lineages (Bandler et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018), as well as projection neuron populations with distinct targets in the hindbrain (Jensen et al., 2008; Robertson et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Embryonic progenitor zone origin has been shown to predict projection neuron populations with distinct targets in the hindbrain.
source: Embryonic progenitor zone origin has been shown to predict subtype identity within other forebrain lineages (Bandler et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2018), as well as projection neuron populations with distinct targets in the hindbrain (Jensen et al., 2008; Robertson et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: All BFCNs arise from the Nkx2.1+ domain within the ventral telencephalon, which encompasses both the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) and preoptic area (POA).
source: Previous work has shown that all BFCNs arise from the Nkx2.1+ domain within the ventral telencephalon, which encompasses both the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) and preoptic area (POA).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from previous work.

claim: The MGE and POA have distinct patterns of gene expression.
source: These two regions have distinct patterns of gene expression (Flames et al., 2007; Hansen et al., 2013) and have been shown to give rise to discrete populations of neurons (Flandin et al., 2010; Gelman et al., 2011; Gelman et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The MGE and POA have been shown to give rise to discrete populations of neurons.
source: These two regions have distinct patterns of gene expression (Flames et al., 2007; Hansen et al., 2013) and have been shown to give rise to discrete populations of neurons (Flandin et al., 2010; Gelman et al., 2011; Gelman et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Both MGE-derived (Lhx6 lineages) and POA-derived (Shh lineages) populations include both deep- and superficially projecting BFCNs.
source: These fate mapping experiments revealed that both MGE-derived (Lhx6 lineages) and POA-derived (Shh lineages) include both deep- and superficially projecting BFCNs, with no statistically significant difference in layer projection density between the two populations (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from spatial fate mapping experiments shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: There is no statistically significant difference in layer projection density between MGE-derived and POA-derived cholinergic populations.
source: These fate mapping experiments revealed that both MGE-derived (Lhx6 lineages) and POA-derived (Shh lineages) include both deep- and superficially projecting BFCNs, with no statistically significant difference in layer projection density between the two populations (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The MGE-derived population gives rise to a slightly higher proportion of cells within the medial septum (Bregma +0.5 to +1.25, p=0.0018).
source: The labeled BFCNs from both the MGE and POA had cell bodies distributed throughout all nuclei of the basal forebrain, although we found that the MGE-derived population gave rise to a slightly higher proportion of cells within the medial septum (Bregma +0.5 to +1.25, p=0.0018) (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: MGE-derived and POA-derived cholinergic populations have comparable projection densities across other cholinergic target regions, including the hippocampus.
source: Despite this, the two populations had comparable projection densities across other cholinergic target regions, including the hippocampus, a major target of the medial septum (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Spatial origin from the MGE versus POA is not a major source of cholinergic neuron diversity with regards to layer specificity, general projection target, or cell body location.
source: These results led us to conclude that spatial origin from the MGE versus POA is not a major source of cholinergic neuron diversity with regards to layer specificity, general projection target, or cell body location.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on spatial fate mapping.

claim: Cellular birthdate is a source of neuronal diversity evident in the ordering of pyramidal neurons within cortical laminae.
source: An alternative source of neuronal diversity during development is cellular birthdate - that is, the timing of a neuronal progenitor cell becoming terminally postmitotic. This principle is evident in the ordering of pyramidal neurons (Angevine and Sidman, 1961) and interneurons (Inan et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2007) within cortical laminae.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on pyramidal neurons.

claim: Cellular birthdate is a source of neuronal diversity evident in the ordering of interneurons within cortical laminae.
source: An alternative source of neuronal diversity during development is cellular birthdate - that is, the timing of a neuronal progenitor cell becoming terminally postmitotic. This principle is evident in the ordering of pyramidal neurons (Angevine and Sidman, 1961) and interneurons (Inan et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2007) within cortical laminae.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on interneurons.

claim: Ascl1 is a proneural gene broadly but transiently expressed in newly born neurons within the ventral embryonic telencephalon.
source: Ascl1 is a proneural gene broadly but transiently expressed in newly born neurons within the ventral embryonic telencephalon (Casarosa et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The expression trajectory of Ascl1 is closely tied to cellular birthdate, with its expression peaking as MGE-, septal, and POA-derived progenitors exit the cell cycle, after which it is rapidly downregulated.
source: The expression trajectory of Ascl1 is closely tied to cellular birthdate, in that its expression peaks as MGE-, septal, and POA-derived progenitors exit the cell cycle, after which it is rapidly downregulated.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about Ascl1 expression dynamics.

claim: Cholinergic neurons projecting to the somatosensory cortex are generally born between E10-E12.
source: Neurons projecting to the somatosensory cortex are generally born between E10-E12, while those labeled at E13 do not send projections to the somatosensory cortex (or most other cortical regions) with the exception of the medial prefrontal cortex (see below) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cholinergic neurons labeled at E13 do not send projections to the somatosensory cortex (or most other cortical regions) with the exception of the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: Neurons projecting to the somatosensory cortex are generally born between E10-E12, while those labeled at E13 do not send projections to the somatosensory cortex (or most other cortical regions) with the exception of the medial prefrontal cortex (see below) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cholinergic neurons that become postmitotic on different days have distinct projection patterns within the primary somatosensory cortex, with early-born neurons projecting to deep layers and later born neurons projecting progressively more superficially.
source: Further analysis revealed that cholinergic neurons that become postmitotic on different days have distinct projection patterns within the primary somatosensory cortex, with early-born neurons projecting to deep layers and later born neurons projecting progressively more superficially (ANOVA, F(4, 22)=48.20, p<0.0001). (Figure 3C,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis (ANOVA) shown in Figure 3C,E.

claim: Axonal projections from E10-born cholinergic cells were predominantly located in L5-6 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
source: Axonal projections from E10-born cells were predominantly located in L5-6, while those from E11-born cells were primarily in L2-4, and those from E12-born cells were almost exclusively found in L1 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Axonal projections from E11-born cholinergic cells were primarily in L2-4 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
source: Axonal projections from E10-born cells were predominantly located in L5-6, while those from E11-born cells were primarily in L2-4, and those from E12-born cells were almost exclusively found in L1 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Axonal projections from E12-born cholinergic cells were almost exclusively found in L1 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
source: Axonal projections from E10-born cells were predominantly located in L5-6, while those from E11-born cells were primarily in L2-4, and those from E12-born cells were almost exclusively found in L1 of the primary somatosensory cortex.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Visual cortex (V1) shows similar characteristics to S1, with cholinergic neurons born at later timepoints innervating progressively more superficial layers.
source: Importantly, we found that V1 shows similar characteristics to S1. Cholinergic neurons born at later timepoints innervate progressively more superficial layers of V1 and, like in S1, those born at E12 predominantly project to layer 1 (ANOVA, F(4, 24)=12.95, p<0.0001, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Cholinergic neurons born at E12 predominantly project to layer 1 of V1.
source: Importantly, we found that V1 shows similar characteristics to S1. Cholinergic neurons born at later timepoints innervate progressively more superficial layers of V1 and, like in S1, those born at E12 predominantly project to layer 1 (ANOVA, F(4, 24)=12.95, p<0.0001, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: M1 and mPFC show relatively weak layer-specificity overall, suggesting that the layer-specificity of cholinergic projections is more prominent in primary sensory areas compared to non-sensory areas.
source: M1 and mPFC, conversely, show relatively weak layer-specificity overall, suggesting that the layer-specificity of cholinergic projections is more prominent in primary sensory areas compared to non-sensory areas.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing sensory and non-sensory areas.

claim: In M1, while E10-born cholinergic cells project primarily to L5/6, those born at E11 and E12 project across layers fairly indiscriminately.
source: In M1, while E10-born cells project primarily to L5/6, those born at E11 and E12 project across layers fairly indiscriminately (ANOVA (F(4, 14)=2.514, p=0.0888), Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: In mPFC, early born cholinergic cells primarily innervate deep layers, while later born cells appear to target all layers.
source: Likewise, in mPFC, which is unique amongst cortical areas in receiving projections from E13 born cholinergic neurons, early born cells primarily innervate deep layers, while later born cells appear to target all layers (ANOVA F(6, 22)=5.678, p=0.0011; Figure 4A,D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4A,D,E.

claim: mPFC is unique amongst cortical areas in receiving projections from E13 born cholinergic neurons.
source: Likewise, in mPFC, which is unique amongst cortical areas in receiving projections from E13 born cholinergic neurons, early born cells primarily innervate deep layers, while later born cells appear to target all layers (ANOVA F(6, 22)=5.678, p=0.0011; Figure 4A,D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,D,E.

claim: Hippocampally projecting cholinergic neurons are primarily born at later timepoints (E12 and E13).
source: We found that hippocampally projecting cholinergic neurons are primarily born at later timepoints (E12 and E13) (hippocampus – ANOVA, F(3,14) = 17.51, p<0.0001, Figure 4B,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4B,F.

claim: Cholinergic neurons projecting to the basolateral amygdala (BLA) are primarily born at E11 and E12.
source: Conversely, those projecting to the basolateral amygdala (BLA) are primarily born at E11 and E12 (ANOVA, F(3,11) = 5.691, p=0.0133).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: BFCNs born at E10 predominantly project to the central amygdala.
source: Interestingly, BFCNs born at E10 predominantly project to the central amygdala, which receives much less overall cholinergic innervation than the BLA (ANOVA, F(3, 25)=308.5, p<0.0001) (Figure 4C,G,H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4C,G,H.

claim: The central amygdala receives much less overall cholinergic innervation than the BLA.
source: Interestingly, BFCNs born at E10 predominantly project to the central amygdala, which receives much less overall cholinergic innervation than the BLA (ANOVA, F(3, 25)=308.5, p<0.0001) (Figure 4C,G,H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4C,G,H.

claim: The cell bodies of cholinergic neurons born at each timepoint were found across the rostral-caudal extent of the basal forebrain.
source: The cell bodies of cholinergic neurons born at each timepoint were found across the rostral-caudal extent of the basal forebrain (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: There is a general trend that early born (and deep-layer projecting) cholinergic cells are biased toward the caudal-most structures, while later born (and more superficially projecting) neurons are found more rostrally.
source: We noted a general trend that early born (and deep-layer projecting) cells were biased toward the caudal-most structures, while later born (and more superficially projecting) neurons were found more rostrally.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data on cell body distribution.

claim: The difference in rostral-caudal distribution of cholinergic cell bodies by birthdate was not statistically significant using tamoxifen birthdating (ANOVA, F (6, 30)=2.103, p=0.0825).
source: However, this difference was not statistically significant (ANOVA, F (6, 30)=2.103, p=0.0825).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The difference in rostral-caudal distribution of cholinergic cell bodies by birthdate reached statistical significance using EdU birthdating (ANOVA, F (6, 24)=3.705, p=0.0092).
source: We repeated this experiment with EdU, an alternative birthdating method that labels cell nuclei, and saw a similar trend that did reach statistical significance (ANOVA, F (6, 24)=3.705, p=0.0092; Figure C, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Previous studies have described several routes that cholinergic axons take when traversing the basal forebrain to reach the cortex.
source: Previous studies have described several routes that cholinergic axons take when traversing the basal forebrain to reach the cortex.
evidence: This is based on knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Cholinergic axonal pathways have been linked to projection target specificity.
source: These axonal pathways have been linked to projection target specificity (Bloem et al., 2014; Eckenstein et al., 1988; Saper, 1984).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: E10 born cholinergic neurons preferentially travel via the caudolateral pathway to reach deep cortical layers.
source: We found that E10 born cholinergic neurons preferentially travel via the caudolateral pathway to reach deep cortical layers (ANOVA, (F(3,8 = 5.799), p=0.0209)) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: E11 born cholinergic neurons have most fibers in the rostrolateral and septal pathways.
source: Those born at E11, which primarily project to layers 2–4, were found to have most fibers in the rostrolateral and septal pathways, suggesting these axons reach the cortex via either route (ANOVA, F(3,12) = 20.14, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: E12 born cholinergic neurons primarily travel medially through the septal pathway.
source: E12 and E13 born neurons, conversely, primarily travel medially through the septal pathway (E12) (ANOVA, F(3,8) = 13.63, p=0.0016) or the rostro-medial pathway (E13) (ANOVA, F(3,8) = 5.599, p=0.0230).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: E13 born cholinergic neurons primarily travel through the rostro-medial pathway.
source: E12 and E13 born neurons, conversely, primarily travel medially through the septal pathway (E12) (ANOVA, F(3,8) = 13.63, p=0.0016) or the rostro-medial pathway (E13) (ANOVA, F(3,8) = 5.599, p=0.0230).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: Cholinergic neurons projecting to deep layers of the somatosensory cortex reach their targets by traversing through the lateral route.
source: Together, these results suggest that cholinergic neurons projecting to deep layers of the somatosensory cortex reach their targets by traversing through the lateral route, while the L1-specific cholinergic neurons reach it via the septal pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pathway analysis data.

claim: L1-specific cholinergic neurons reach the somatosensory cortex via the septal pathway.
source: Together, these results suggest that cholinergic neurons projecting to deep layers of the somatosensory cortex reach their targets by traversing through the lateral route, while the L1-specific cholinergic neurons reach it via the septal pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pathway analysis data.

claim: E13 born cholinergic neurons do not target most of the cortex outside of the mPFC, and reach this target via the rostro-medial route.
source: E13 born neurons do not target most of the cortex outside of the mPFC, and reach this target via the rostro-medial route.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from birthdating and pathway analysis.

claim: Axons traveling via the septal route primarily arborize within superficial layers, particularly layer 1, of the somatosensory cortex.
source: Quantification of cholinergic projections within the somatosensory cortex labeled using this method confirmed that axons traveling via the septal route primarily arborize within superficial layers, particularly layer 1 (Figure 6C,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from pathway-specific CAV-2::Cre injections shown in Figure 6C,E.

claim: Axons traveling via the caudolateral route are relatively restricted to deep layers of the somatosensory cortex.
source: Conversely, those traveling via the caudolateral route are relatively restricted to deep layers (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from pathway-specific CAV-2::Cre injections shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Early born cholinergic neurons project their axons via the caudolateral route to innervate deep layers of somatosensory cortex.
source: Together, these results indicate that early born cholinergic neurons project their axons via the caudolateral route to innervate deep layers of somatosensory cortex, while the axons of later born cells traverse the septal route to innervate superficial layers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pathway analysis and birthdating data.

claim: The axons of later born cholinergic cells traverse the septal route to innervate superficial layers of somatosensory cortex.
source: Together, these results indicate that early born cholinergic neurons project their axons via the caudolateral route to innervate deep layers of somatosensory cortex, while the axons of later born cells traverse the septal route to innervate superficial layers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pathway analysis and birthdating data.

claim: Cholinergic neurons targeting the somatosensory cortex innervate specific layers, an organizational principle that was previously unknown.
source: Here, we show that cholinergic neurons targeting the somatosensory cortex innervate specific layers – an organizational principle that was previously unknown and likely significantly contributes to the laminar specificity of cholinergic signaling (Muñoz and Rudy, 2014; Muñoz et al., 2017; Obermayer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The layer-specific organization of cholinergic neurons likely significantly contributes to the laminar specificity of cholinergic signaling.
source: Here, we show that cholinergic neurons targeting the somatosensory cortex innervate specific layers – an organizational principle that was previously unknown and likely significantly contributes to the laminar specificity of cholinergic signaling (Muñoz and Rudy, 2014; Muñoz et al., 2017; Obermayer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and cited literature.

claim: The layer specificity of cholinergic projections is determined by the birthdate of cholinergic neurons in the BF.
source: Furthermore, we found that this specificity is determined by the birthdate of cholinergic neurons in the BF, with early born cholinergic neurons primarily targeting deep layers and later born neurons targeting progressively superficial layers of the somatosensory cortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: A population of cholinergic neurons exists whose axonal projections are almost completely restricted to layer 1.
source: Importantly, we identified a population of cholinergic neurons whose axonal projections are almost completely restricted to layer 1.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Cholinergic neuronal birthdate is correlated with projection topography in other target regions, including other cortical areas, hippocampus, and amygdala.
source: Cholinergic neuronal birthdate is also correlated with projection topography in other target regions, including other cortical areas, hippocampus, and amygdala.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: Cholinergic neurons born at different times project via distinct axonal pathways to reach their targets.
source: Finally, we found that cholinergic neurons born at different times project via distinct axonal pathways to reach their targets.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from pathway analysis.

claim: The existence of layer-specific cholinergic neurons has been previously hypothesized given the distinct actions of ACh in different cortical laminae.
source: Given the distinct actions of ACh in different cortical laminae, the existence of layer-specific cholinergic neurons has been previously hypothesized.
evidence: This is based on inference from known distinct actions of ACh in different layers.

claim: The population of cholinergic neurons born at E12 that almost exclusively innervate layer 1 may explain the high density of cholinergic axons in L1 compared to other layers.
source: This population may explain the high density of cholinergic axons in L1 compared to other layers.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: The L1-specific cholinergic population has important functional implications for ACh in cortical processes regulated by L1, such as cross-modal signaling.
source: Moreover, it has important functional implications for ACh in cortical processes regulated by L1, such as cross-modal signaling.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional implications of the findings.

claim: Marked differences exist in the degree of innervation specificity within sensory (S1 and V1) and non-sensory (mPFC and M1) cortical regions.
source: Importantly, we observed marked differences in the degree of innervation specificity within sensory (S1 and V1) and non-sensory (mPFC and M1) cortical regions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing different cortical regions.

claim: A recent anterograde tracing study showed that labeled cohorts of cholinergic neurons targeting the mPFC could be divided into two groups: one group projecting to all layers, and another projecting to deep layers only.
source: In a recent anterograde tracing study, it was shown that labeled cohorts of cholinergic neurons targeting the mPFC could be divided into two groups: one group projecting to all layers, and another projecting to deep layers only (Bloem et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The current study's results corroborate the finding that cholinergic projections to mPFC include both layer-specific and non-specific populations.
source: Our results corroborate this finding: projections from early born cholinergic neurons are relatively restricted to deeper layers, while projections from later born cells were visible across all layers of mPFC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the current study that agrees with previous findings.

claim: The discrepancy between the degree of innervation specificity observed in sensory versus non-sensory areas may relate to the distinct roles of cholinergic signaling in information flow within these regions (bottom-up versus top-down, respectively).
source: This discrepancy between the degree of innervation specificity observed in sensory versus non-sensory areas may relate to the distinct roles of cholinergic signaling in information flow within these regions (bottom-up versus top-down, respectively).
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of the observed differences.

claim: A recent study fate mapped cholinergic neurons arising from the embryonic septum, another Nkx2.1+ region, and found that the septum gives rise to cholinergic neurons whose axons have no apparent specificity within the cortex.
source: Complementing our results, a recent study fate mapped cholinergic neurons arising from the embryonic septum, another Nkx2.1+ region. Like the MGE and POA, the septum gives rise to cholinergic neurons whose axons have no apparent specificity within the cortex (Magno et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The broad embryonic zones (MGE, POA, septum) all produce heterogenous populations of cholinergic neurons that, as a group, project throughout the forebrain.
source: Together, these results show that these broad embryonic zones all produce heterogenous populations of cholinergic neurons that, as a group, project throughout the forebrain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current study's data and cited literature.

claim: It is possible that smaller, more specific subregions of the embryonic structures could give rise to populations of cholinergic neurons with more defined projection topography.
source: However, we cannot rule out the possibility that smaller, more specific subregions of these embryonic structures could give rise to populations of cholinergic neurons with more defined projection topography.
evidence: This is speculation about possibilities not ruled out by the current study.

claim: Cellular birthdate defines subpopulations of cholinergic neurons with distinct projection distributions.
source: By contrast, we discovered that cellular birthdate defines subpopulations of cholinergic neurons with distinct projection distributions.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from birthdating experiments.

claim: It is unclear whether cholinergic populations are specified as 'deep layer-targeting' or 'superficial layer-targeting' as soon as they become postmitotic or whether this reflects temporal shifts in guidance cues that both dictate their projection trajectory and laminar specificity.
source: How this specificity is achieved is unclear. Are cholinergic populations specified as 'deep layer-targeting' or 'superficial layer-targeting' as soon as they become postmitotic or do these reflect temporal shifts in guidance cues that both dictate their projection trajectory and laminar specificity?
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms underlying the observed specificity.

claim: Heterochronic transplantation of birthdated, postmitotic cholinergic neurons could potentially discern between specification at birth versus temporal guidance cues.
source: Although at present prohibitively challenging, one could potentially discern between these possibilities through heterochronic transplantation of birthdated, postmitotic cholinergic neurons.
evidence: This is speculation about a potential experimental approach.

claim: Cholinergic projections could initially project broadly across cortical laminae and become refined to specific layers through a combination of synaptic pruning and programmed cell death.
source: Furthermore, cholinergic projections could initially project broadly across cortical laminae and become refined to specific layers through a combination of synaptic pruning and programmed cell death.
evidence: This is speculation about potential developmental mechanisms.

claim: In cholinergic neurons, both synaptic pruning and programmed cell death are regulated in part by the p75 neurotrophin receptor.
source: In cholinergic neurons, both these processes are regulated in part by the p75 neurotrophin receptor (Barrett, 2000; Boskovic et al., 2019; Niewiadomska et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Attractant or repellant cues secreted from cortical cells could play a key role in guiding cholinergic fibers to the appropriate layers.
source: Additionally, attractant or repellant cues secreted from cortical cells could play a key role in guiding cholinergic fibers to the appropriate layers.
evidence: This is speculation about potential guidance mechanisms.

claim: The 'inside-out' innervation pattern of cholinergic neurons reflects the manner in which the cortex itself is generated.
source: This is a particularly compelling idea given that the 'inside-out' innervation pattern of cholinergic neurons observed here reflects the manner in which the cortex itself is generated (Angevine and Sidman, 1961).
evidence: This is an inference based on the parallel between cholinergic innervation pattern and cortical development, supported by a citation.

claim: Cholinergic diversity likely extends beyond differences in their axonal targeting, with subpopulations possessing distinct functional and electrophysiological properties.
source: Cholinergic diversity likely extends beyond differences in their axonal targeting, with subpopulations possessing distinct functional and electrophysiological properties.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings and general principles of neuronal diversity.

claim: A recently published study suggests that different basal forebrain cholinergic cell types are responsible for the two timescales of ACh release in the cortex, with one mediating slow, volume transmission and the other characterized by phasic, point-to-point release.
source: For example, a recently published study suggests that different basal forebrain cholinergic cell types are responsible for the two timescales of ACh release in the cortex, with one mediating slow, volume transmission and the other characterized by phasic, point-to-point release (Laszlovszky et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Cholinergic neurons directly within the globus pallidus are more intimately involved in basal ganglia circuitry and have specialized firing properties when compared to their neighbors in the nucleus basalis.
source: Additionally, it has recently been shown that cholinergic neurons directly within the globus pallidus are more intimately involved in basal ganglia circuitry and have specialized firing properties when compared to their neighbors in the nucleus basalis (Saunders et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Cholinergic neurons in the pedunculopontine and laterodorsal tegmental nuclei of the brainstem innervate the basal ganglia and thalamus, but do not appear to directly innervate most cortical areas.
source: For example, cholinergic neurons in the pedunculopontine and laterodorsal tegmental nuclei of the brainstem innervate the basal ganglia and thalamus, but do not appear to directly innervate most cortical areas (Huerta-Ocampo et al., 2020; Martinez-Gonzalez et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A population of ChAT+ interneurons are found within the cortex.
source: In addition, a population of ChAT+interneurons are found within the cortex, although until recently it was unclear whether these cells actually release ACh.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cortical interneurons.

claim: Recent work has shown that a subset of cortical ChAT+ interneurons do appear to in some capacity release ACh.
source: Recent work, however, has shown that a subset of these cells do appear to in some capacity release ACh (Granger et al., 2020; Obermayer et al., 2019), although their functional role has yet to be fully resolved.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: The functional role of cortical ChAT+ interneurons has yet to be fully resolved.
source: Recent work, however, has shown that a subset of these cells do appear to in some capacity release ACh (Granger et al., 2020; Obermayer et al., 2019), although their functional role has yet to be fully resolved.
evidence: This is based on the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Recent advances in single-cell genomics technologies should provide useful insight into the full diversity of forebrain cholinergic neurons.
source: The recent advances in single-cell genomics technologies should provide useful insight into the full diversity of forebrain cholinergic neurons.
evidence: This is speculation about future research directions.

claim: 95% of ChAT+ neurons in the striatum identified by anti-ChAT IHC co-express tdTomato in ChatFlpO; Dlx6aCre; Rosa26Ai65 brains.
source: (A) Striatum: 95% of ChAT+ neurons identified by anti-ChAT IHC co-express tdTomato (527/555 cells counted).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 99% of ChAT+ neurons in the medial septum/diagonal band identified by anti-ChAT IHC co-express tdTomato in ChatFlpO; Dlx6aCre; Rosa26Ai65 brains.
source: (B) Medial septum/diagonal band: 99% (576/580 cells counted).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 97% of ChAT+ neurons in the diagonal band/substantia innominata/nucleus basalis identified by anti-ChAT IHC co-express tdTomato in ChatFlpO; Dlx6aCre; Rosa26Ai65 brains.
source: (C–D) Diagonal band/substantia innominata/nucleus basalis: 97% (437/449 cells counted).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: The soma of the L1-targeting cholinergic cell was located in the rostral substantia innominata.
source: The soma of the L1-targeting cell was located in the rostral substantia innominata, sending its axon rostrally then dorsally through the medial septum, ultimately entering the cortex through L1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: The L1-targeting cholinergic cell sends its axon rostrally then dorsally through the medial septum, ultimately entering the cortex through L1.
source: The soma of the L1-targeting cell was located in the rostral substantia innominata, sending its axon rostrally then dorsally through the medial septum, ultimately entering the cortex through L1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: The L1-targeting cholinergic cell had arborizations extending from the caudal motor cortex to the rostral visual cortex, almost entirely restricted to layer 1.
source: Despite the fact that this cell had arborizations extending from the caudal motor cortex to the rostral visual cortex, it was almost entirely restricted to layer 1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: The soma of the L5/6-targeting cholinergic cell was located in the nucleus basalis, near the globus pallidus.
source: Conversely, the soma of the L5/6-targeting cell was located in the nucleus basalis, near the globus pallidus.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: The L5/6-targeting cholinergic cell's axon traversed through the striatum to enter the external capsule before entering the somatosensory cortex from L6.
source: Its axon traversed through the striatum to enter the external capsule before entering the somatosensory cortex from L6.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: The arborizations of the L5/6-targeting cholinergic cell were restricted to the somatosensory cortex and covered a much more limited rostral to caudal territory compared to the L1-targeting cell.
source: Unlike the L1-targeting cell, the arborizations of the L5/6-targeting cell were restricted to the somatosensory cortex and covered a much more limited rostral to caudal territory.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from single-cell reconstruction.

claim: Both deep- and superficial-targeting cholinergic neurons can reside within one of several nuclei across the rostral-caudal axis of the basal forebrain, including the vertical diagonal band (vDB), horizontal diagonal band (hDB), substantia innominata (SI), and nucleus basalis (NB).
source: We found that both deep- and superficial-targeting cholinergic neurons can reside within one of several nuclei across the rostral-caudal axis of the basal forebrain, including the vertical diagonal band (vDB), horizontal diagonal band (hDB), substantia innominata (SI), and nucleus basalis (NB).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from soma location mapping.
